rows.basis: Cloud services 68,753,609 + colocation services 8,913,816 = 77,667,425, the two HPC segments the thesis names. Digital asset mining (27.3M) and ETH staking (7.0M) are excluded. The cloud business sits in WhiteFiber, which is about 70.5% owned and consolidated; the full segment is counted.
Cloud services 45,727,735 + colocation services 1,361,241 (Enovum, acquired October 2024) = 47,088,976. Mining (58.6M) and ETH staking (1.8M) are excluded.

The FY2024 MD&A cites a GPU contract worth more than $50M of annualized revenue (a run-rate, not a fiscal-year figure), a 300-GPU order worth about $0.9M per year over five years, and a $20.2M aggregate revenue opportunity (a contract total). None of these is a FY2025 revenue forecast, so no amount is given.

Growth in gross cloud service equipment (GPU servers): 146,589,318 − 63,360,624 = 83,228,694. The following are excluded: colocation service equipment growth of 19,365,682 (only one category is allowed), construction in progress (up 132.4M, use not stated), leasehold improvements, and miners. The figure is net of any disposals, so it is likely a floor on HPC spend.

A purchase order for 130 H200 servers for about $30M, stated in the FY2024 MD&A. The share is taken against FY2025 consolidated capex of 285,928,406. This purchase is likely already inside the FY2025 growth in cloud service equipment.
